segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One day Peter came to Jesus with a question that had been sitting heavy on his heart. It was about forgiveness — and about someone who kept hurting him.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Lord, he asked, how many times do I have to forgive my brother when he keeps sinning against me? Would seven times be enough? Peter must have thought he was being generous.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In other words, stop counting. Real forgiveness doesn't keep a ledger. And then, to show them what he meant, Jesus told a story.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: There was once a king who decided to settle his accounts. One by one, his servants were brought in to answer for what they owed him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One man was dragged forward who owed the king ten thousand talents. It was a staggering fortune — more money than a working man could earn in ten thousand lifetimes. A debt like that could never, ever be repaid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The man had nothing to pay with. So the king ordered that he be sold — his wife, his children, everything he owned — to recover even a fraction of it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The servant threw himself down on the ground and begged. Please, he cried, be patient with me, and I will pay back everything!

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the king looked at this desperate man crumpled before him — and his heart broke with compassion. He did something no one expected.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He didn't just give him more time. He cancelled the whole debt. Every last coin of that impossible fortune — forgiven, wiped away, gone. The man was free.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But then that same servant walked outside. And there he found one of his fellow servants — a man who owed him a hundred silver coins. A few months' wages. Real money, yes — but nothing next to the ocean he'd just been forgiven.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He grabbed the man by the throat and started to choke him. Pay me what you owe me! he snarled. Pay me now!

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Pay me that thou owest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him with the very same words he himself had used only moments before: Please, be patient with me, and I will pay you back!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he refused. He would not listen. He had the man thrown into prison until he could pay back every penny.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The other servants saw the whole thing, and it grieved them deeply. They went and told the king everything that had happened.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The king summoned him back. You wicked servant! he said. I forgave you that enormous debt because you begged me to. Shouldn't you have shown the same mercy to your fellow servant that I showed to you?

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And in his anger the king handed him over to be punished until he should pay back all that he owed. Then Jesus turned the story toward every one of us.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Here is the whole point of the story. Look at the two debts side by side. The mountain that was forgiven us, and the small handful we're asked to forgive each other. They aren't even close.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: We forgive the small things because of the mountain we've been forgiven. To be handed an ocean of mercy, and then choke someone over a cup of it — that is the one thing this King cannot bear.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You were forgiven a debt you could never repay. Who is holding a small one against you — that you could let go of today?
